summary.name: Downright
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source native Markdown editor and viewer for macOS that renders Markdown files as documents, edits their exact source, and previews them in Finder.
use_cases: preview Markdown files in Finder with Space
edit Markdown source while seeing a rendered view
review changes made to a file by coding agents or other apps
read Markdown notes with math and diagrams
render Markdown from the terminal with the down command
summary.what_it_does: Downright opens ordinary Markdown files and renders them as Mac documents while keeping the exact source editable in the same window. It supports math, Mermaid diagrams, pipe tables, GitHub-style alerts, footnotes, task lists, and syntax-coloured code blocks. It previews files in Finder via Quick Look and can be piped through the down command. When another app or coding agent rewrites an open file, it marks changes and protects unsaved edits, and it keeps a timeline of versions. The page states that the app adds styling without changing the file's bytes and sends no app telemetry.
notable: Open source under MIT license with no WebView, per the page
Renders Markdown in Finder Quick Look and includes a raw source view
Watches externally edited files, highlights changes and protects unsaved edits
Version timeline for comparing any two versions of a file
caveats: Page includes self-reported benchmarks on a single unrecorded machine (historical baseline, not cross-machine claims)
